D014_m001.question:
Honestly, I feel like I’ve been running on empty for a long time now… about two years, maybe a bit over that. I still run my design firm, I show up to client meetings, I put on the blazer and the lipstick, but underneath I’m just… tired. Not “I need a vacation” tired — it’s this bone-deep exhaustion that doesn’t lift, even if I sleep in or take a weekend off. 

I find myself tearing up over the smallest things. A fabric sample reminds me of an old project, a song in the car, a comment from a colleague — and suddenly I’m fighting back tears in the bathroom. It’s embarrassing, especially when I’m supposed to be the poised one in the room.

What worries me is that I’ve sort of given up on the idea that it can get better. I still do all the “right” things — yoga, green juice, therapy apps — but I don’t believe any of it will really change how I feel. It’s like I’m watching my life from the outside, going through the motions, and assuming this low, gray version of me is just how it’s going to be from now on.

A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder

D014_m002.question:

I’m exhausted all the time. Standing at the counter, counting cash, talking to people—things I’ve done for years—feel like I’m dragging myself through mud. When I get home, I just collapse on the couch. The laundry piles up, I cook less, I’m behind on little things like paying bills on time, even though I work at a bank.

What scares me is I’ve kind of stopped believing anything will really get better. I still go through the motions—go to work, help with the kids—but in my head I’m thinking, “This is just how it is now.” My husband asks what’s wrong, and I don’t even know what to say anymore.
